registry_info.name: generator_bench
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `generator` family (simplex - perlin - value - cellular). Four bases evaluated at the same 2304 positions and stood in the same body, so the basis is the only variable. The transpose of noise_quarry.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The four basis names are PRELOADED from noiseroom.gd at runtime and validated at _ready in both directions, and the evidence ladder is preloaded from noise_quarry.gd the same way; do not retype either here or in the script.

generator_bench.name: Generator Bench
generator_bench.description: Four generators, one body. Simplex, perlin, value and cellular are evaluated at the SAME 2304 positions on the same lattice cut, scaled by the same gain against the same fixed gauge, and stood in the same body — a 1.20 m crust of 48 x 48 tiles whose height is the sample — so the four benches differ by the basis and by nothing else. Three of them are smooth fields; the fourth is not an interpolation at all but distance to the nearest of a set of feature points, and it is the one with edges in it. `octaves` changes how many scales are summed into each field, which is also how much of each basis's own character survives the summing. `evidence` changes how much proof is standing that the four were asked the same question — nothing, a datum rule across all four at the field's zero, or a counted census of each bench's own 2304 samples on the board behind it. The transpose of noise_quarry, which holds one field and cuts it three ways. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
interactions: stand square to the rank and look along the four skylines: three of them swell and one of them has creases
find the cellular bench's straight edges — they are cell boundaries, and no other bench has a straight edge anywhere
read the datum rule across all four: the cellular field sits mostly above it and the value field mostly below, and neither is a bug
switch octaves from 1 to 3 and watch the four benches become harder to tell apart, which is what summing scales does

compare the four censuses: the one that separates value and cellular from the rest cannot separate simplex from perlin, because what separates those two is the shape of the lattice and not the spread of the numbers
generator_bench.qfep_connection: Four constructions for one question — what number is at this position — and no neutral one among them. Each carries its lattice into its answer: perlin's square grid stays faintly latent because the value is zero at every corner, value noise's grid stops being latent and becomes the picture, simplex's triangular lattice leaves no preferred direction at all, and cellular has no interpolation to hide a lattice inside — it partitions. The bench's own dark spot is the census: it is the artifact's most rigorous apparatus and it is blind to exactly the difference the artifact is named for. simplex and perlin have near-identical distributions and completely different geometries, so the most carefully counted evidence in the frame is the evidence that cannot see the headline case. That is drawn rather than hidden: the two censuses stand side by side looking alike above two crusts that do not.
generator_bench.relationships: Synthesised from the six registry names that declare `generator` over five scenes: perlin_noise, noise_terrain, noise_space, shader_noise_space, and voxel_noise_demo / marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo, which are one scene under two names. Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside. The TRANSPOSE of noise_quarry: the quarry exhibits `readout` and varies the field, this exhibits `generator` and varies the field's maker, and both sweep evidence x octaves so the two sheets can be laid side by side. Sibling in argument to slack_yard, which makes the same move for the `slack` family.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 5.58 m across the four benches by 2.17 m from the census board to the front edge, so a 6 x 3 clear patch — one cell wider than noise_quarry, which is the cost of a fourth bench. The basis names are lettered on the apron's +Z edge, the datum rule stands at +Z and the board closes the -Z side, so the artifact reads correctly approached from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. `wall_backing` is true because the artifact BRINGS its own board and should not be given a second wall 0.4 m behind it. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through the benches — correct, because there are no benches, there is a picture of four.
spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 5.58 m, h 1.06 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the same geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts: BoxMesh slabs (apron, two board halves, two posts, the datum rule, up to 32 census bars) and four SurfaceTool ArrayMesh crusts. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D and no CSG, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present; the four Label3D basis tabs are not MeshInstance3D and do not enter the box. X = 4 x 1.20 benches + 3 x 0.18 gaps + 2 x 0.12 apron margin = 5.58. Z = -1.27 (apron behind the board) to +0.90 (apron front edge) = 2.17. Y = 0 (apron underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 1.06 = the board's top. THE BOX IS THE SAME AT ALL NINE TILES: the apron and the board define all six faces and neither moves, the datum rule sits inside them (y 0.27-0.34, z 0.849-0.871) and the census bars sit inside them (y 0.58-1.06, z -1.125 to -1.105), so the camera is identical across the sheet. The crust cannot reach either bound either: its gauge is built so h = -1 lands exactly on the apron top (DATUM - AMP = Y_FLOOR = 0.10) and h = +1 lands exactly on the board's lower edge (DATUM + AMP = BAND_Y0 = 0.58), and the widest realised |h| in the whole sheet is 0.95431.

dna.axis_shape:
THREE WORDS, TWO SHAPES, AND THE FAMILY WORD IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT AN AXIS.

`generator` SITS SIDE BY SIDE, which is why it is exhibited and not swept, and the evidence is in the six members' CODE rather than their prose. In five of the six the word is spent by a flat four-branch dispatch returning four mutually exclusive FastNoiseLite enum constants: _noise_type_for() at noiseterrain.gd:128, VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd:147 and NoiseVisualizer.gd:119, and the same four branches written inline in NoiseSpace._build_noise (NoiseSpace.gd:87-97). In the sixth the word is an INDEX written into one shader uniform, and QueerNoiseShader.gdshader's noise2d() dispatches on it with three ifs and a fallthrough. No branch contains another. No value is another value plus a term: a triangular lattice is not a square lattice with something added, and a Voronoi partition is not a smoother interpolation. Parallel values are exactly the case where holding them all at once is NOT merely the top value — it is the object — so the four stand together in every one of the nine tiles, lettered on the apron, and the axes vary something else.

`evidence` NESTS in the ordinary way: result is contained in trace is contained in longhand. _build() adds the datum rule under `if evidence == "trace" or evidence == "longhand"` and the census under `if evidence == "longhand"`; no rung removes a mark an earlier rung drew, and the four crusts are identical at all three. Its tail is a ceiling, not a case.

`octaves` NESTS too, and more literally than a ladder usually does: the K-octave field is the K-1-octave field plus one more term of the same sum. _compute_field() accumulates s += amp * _basis(...) with amp halving each pass, so octave 3 is octave 2 with 0.125 of amplitude added on top. The ONE thing that is not nested is the normaliser — the sum is divided by the sum of the amplitudes it actually used, which differs per rung — and that is deliberate: it keeps every rung at full range so the fixed colour ceiling, the fixed 2 x AMP gauge and the fixed census ceiling mean the same thing in all nine frames. Without it the K=1 field would occupy 57% of the gauge and the K=3 field 100%, and the axis would be measuring loudness rather than detail.
dna.default:
evidence=longhand, octaves=1.

A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom is spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `longhand` AND NOT `result`. `result` is four crusts and no way to say they came from one sampling, which is a picture of four sculptures rather than of an argument. `longhand` is the rung where the artifact's second finding is legible without a caption: cellular's census sits visibly high (mean h +0.156) and value's visibly low (-0.093) against a scale whose zero is drawn as a tonal step in the board, so the reader can see that the four bases do not even agree about where the middle of a field is. A visitor who meets only the default meets that. `trace` is one token away and is the right value for a room that wants the four skylines to dominate.

WHY `1` AND NOT `4`, WHICH IS WHERE THIS BENCH DISAGREES WITH ITS WHOLE FAMILY AND WITH ITS OWN COMPANION. Every member of the family defaults octaves to 4 and noise_quarry took 4 as well, saying "at one octave the field is a single smooth swell and all three bodies read it about equally well, which makes for a handsome frame and a weak argument." That is right for the quarry, whose subject is the BODY: the body needs a busy field to distinguish itself. It is exactly backwards for this bench, whose subject is the BASIS, because summing scales is the operation that makes the four bases hardest to tell apart. Measured, in the critic's own currency, on a homogeneous rank where all four benches carry one basis so only the basis differs: the mean pairwise separation between the four is 20.00% focus at K=1, 18.62% at K=2 and 17.96% at K=3, and the simplex-perlin pair specifically falls 16.92 -> 15.29 -> 14.54. The default is therefore the rung where the artifact's own claim is strongest, and the axis exists to show what is lost by climbing it.

DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, and it is why `evidence` is listed first. build_dna_gallery.sweep walks the axes in declaration order and trims the LATER one from the tail of its value list until the cross product fits the cap. 3 x 3 = 9 fits the gallery's default --max=9 exactly, so nothing is trimmed either way — but if the cap is ever lowered, evidence-first keeps all three evidence rungs and trims octaves from the top, which drops the rung the artifact is weakest at rather than the default it is strongest at.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the six `generator` declarations leave unbuilt: each of them can show you ONE basis at a time in ONE body, so comparing two means walking between two rooms and trusting that the two rooms agree about everything except the basis — which they do not, since they differ in frequency, in octave count, in gauge, in body and in seed. perlin_noise's four values are four tabletops of lifted cubes; noise_space's are four 10 m walkable landforms; voxel_noise_demo's are four marched isosurfaces. Not one of them can stand two bases at once, because a body can only be filled by one function at a time.
dna.kin:
THE FAMILY IS SIX NAMES OVER FIVE SCENES, AND ONE OF THOSE IS THE CORPUS'S USUAL HIDDEN FAMILY. voxel_noise_demo (registry/isosurfaces.json) and marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo (registry/randomness.json) both point at res://algorithms/spacetopology/marchingcubes/voxel_noise_demo.tscn and carry byte-identical axis blocks, fixture and framing. One scene, two names — the tell CLAUDE.md names, and it means `generator` is declared six times and implemented five.

THE VALUE LIST IS NOT DRIFTED. Checked character for character: noiseterrain.gd:109, NoiseSpace.gd:65, VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd:85 and noiseroom.gd:33 all carry `const GENERATORS: PackedStringArray = ["simplex", "perlin", "value", "cellular"]`, in that order; PerlinNoise.gd:40 carries the same four in a comment beside a bare `@export var generator: String`. All six registry entries declare the same four in the same order. There is no owner and no alias table, which is the drift risk — dialect B of `readout` was in exactly this state when noise_quarry found it — so this bench reads the array out of noiseroom.gd at build time rather than copying it, and _check_family_list() push_errors in both directions at _ready: a family value this bench has no basis for, and a basis this bench evaluates that the family has dropped.

WHY noiseroom.gd IS THE ONE PRELOADED. Same test noise_quarry applied to dialect B: it is the only one of the four const-carriers whose script parses with NO external dependency at all — no class_name, no preload, no reference to a global class. noiseterrain.gd is `class_name QueerNoiseTerrain` and types a member as NoiseBlobSpawner; VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd is class_name'd and calls MarchingCubesLookupTables; NoiseSpace.gd is class_name'd and `extends TopologySpace`. Preloading any of those would put another script between this artifact and its own vocabulary. noiseroom.gd is also the member whose four bases this file ports, so one preload does both jobs and the vocabulary and the implementation cannot come apart.

THE DEFAULT VALUE OF `generator` ALREADY DISAGREES ACROSS THE FAMILY, and the bench does not have to take a side because it does not sweep the word: five members default to simplex and shader_noise_space defaults to perlin, on the honest ground that perlin is what its shader has always computed. All four stand here.

ONE DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE INSIDE THE FAMILY, AND THIS BENCH TAKES THE MAJORITY. At `cellular`, voxel_noise_demo additionally sets cellular_return_type = RETURN_CELL_VALUE, and says why: it LEVEL-SETS the field at a fixed iso of 0.5, and FastNoiseLite's default RETURN_DISTANCE is one-sided, so the rung would have moved how MUCH of the box is solid rather than what its structure is. The other four leave the return type alone. This bench DISPLACES a height rather than level-setting one, so it is in the majority's case and takes the majority's answer — distance to the nearest feature point, which is what makes the cellular bench a partition with creases rather than a field of flat plates. voxel_noise_demo is right for a level set and would be wrong here; that is a fact about the two bodies, not about the word.

`evidence` IS THE FAMILY WORD, TAKEN WITH A SUB-LIST THAT ALREADY EXISTS. 47 registry entries declare `evidence` counting this one; of the 46 before it, 28 carry result | trace | longhand | axiom, four carry result | trace | sources | longhand, and SEVEN carry exactly result | trace | longhand in that order: calder_mobile, calder_object_mobile, ftc_bridge, noise_quarry, sine_wave_controller, weather_vector_field, zeno_staircase. This takes the three-rung list, and the literal in the @export_enum hint — which GDScript will not let me compute — is held against noise_quarry.EVIDENCES at _ready in both directions. `axiom` is refused: see dna.declines.

`octaves` IS THE FAMILY WORD AND ITS LIST HAS ALREADY DRIFTED. Seven registry entries declared it before this one, in THREE different value lists: [1, 2, 3, 4] (noise_space, noise_quarry), [1, 2, 4, 6] (simplex_noise) and [1, 2, 3, 6] (marchingcubes_cave / mc_cave and marchingcubes_inside_cave / mc_inside_cave, which are two scenes under four names). Every one of those is a Nyquist argument about ITS OWN grid, so the argument is re-derived here rather than inherited, and it comes out at THREE.

  This bench's crust is 1.20 m across sampled at GRID = 48, i.e. every 0.025 m.
  SPAN = 4.0, so octave k has a lattice cell of 1.20 / (4 * 2^(k-1)) metres:
    k=1  0.3000 m = 12.0 sample cells
    k=2  0.1500 m =  6.0
    k=3  0.0750 m =  3.0
    k=4  0.0375 m =  1.5   <- below the 2-cell Nyquist wavelength
  So the ladder stops at 3 on this grid and the fourth rung is refused on the record.

WHY SPAN IS 4 AND NOT THE QUARRY'S 1, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON THE LADDERS DIFFER. The quarry's subject is the BODY, so one lattice cell across the bench is fine — it wants a single smooth swell that three bodies can each embody. This bench's subject is the LATTICE, and a single cell has no lattice structure to photograph: perlin's square grid, value's plateaus, simplex's absence of a preferred direction and cellular's cell walls are all statements about the arrangement of cells, and you cannot see an arrangement of one. Four cells across is the smallest number that shows an arrangement while leaving 12 sample cells per lattice cell at the base. The two artifacts therefore stop their ladders at the SAME resolution — 3.0 sample cells per finest lattice cell, at k=4 for the quarry and k=3 here — and differ only in where they start.

WHAT A FOURTH RUNG WOULD HAVE COST, in the same currency noise_quarry used. To make a rung named 4 resolve at three sample cells the grid would have to be GRID >= 3 * 4 * 2^3 = 96, i.e. a cell of 0.0125 m, which at this sweep's 115.42 px/m projects to 1.2 screen pixels along the frame's short axis. It would also quadruple the mesh: this bench already commits 4 x 2304 cells x about 18 vertices, and at 96 that is 663,000 vertices built by SurfaceTool in GDScript at every map load. The finer ladder is only available on a grid whose cells are invisible AND whose build is four times as expensive, which is the same trade noise_space made and the reason a three-rung ladder is the honest one here.

WHAT THIS BENCH CAN SHOW THAT THE QUARRY CANNOT, asked for explicitly and answered plainly. noise_quarry holds ONE field — a hand-written integer-hash gradient noise — and cuts it three ways; it refused the `generator` vocabulary outright, so it cannot say anything about a basis at all, and its `octaves` axis is a statement about detail in one function. This bench holds four bases in one body, so it can show (a) that the four disagree about SHAPE, which is the headline, (b) that they disagree about where the middle of a field is, which no single-basis artifact can show because a single basis has no one to disagree with — cellular's 2304 samples have mean h +0.156 and value's -0.093 on the same gauge, and (c) that summing scales moves them TOWARDS each other, which needs two rungs and two bases at once and is invisible to every member of the family. Conversely the quarry can show what this bench cannot: that three CONVENTIONS put zero in three different places. Between them the noise sequence's two questions are factored, and the two sheets share evidence x octaves so they can be laid side by side.

WHERE THIS DISAGREES WITH noise_quarry, AND WHO IS RIGHT. The quarry's decline of `generator` gives as its decisive reason that "in all four members that declare it the word names a FastNoiseLite noise type", and that was already untrue when it was written: shader_noise_space declares the same four values against a hand-written GLSL dispatch, and it is the fifth implementation, not a fourth. The quarry's CONCLUSION stands — one hand-written gradient basis calling itself `perlin` while the other three values have no implementation at all would be the folding_past fault exactly — but its stated reason does not, and the word does not mean "a FastNoiseLite enum". It means "which basis fills the field", and the family already contains a member that answers it without FastNoiseLite. That is what licenses this bench to port rather than to call.

WHY THE BASES ARE PORTED FROM THE SHADER RATHER THAN CALLED FROM FastNoiseLite, and what it costs. Two reasons, both about being able to check the artifact before shipping it, since the bench is forbidden to run Godot. (1) A ported basis is exactly replicable in Python, so dna.predicted_degeneracy below is arithmetic done on this geometry at this camera rather than an estimate; FastNoiseLite's fractal normalisation cannot be reproduced offline, which is the reason noise_quarry gave for hand-writing its own basis. (2) Four bases on ONE fixed gauge only works if their amplitudes are already matched, and FastNoiseLite's four are not — cellular at RETURN_DISTANCE is one-sided, which is precisely why voxel_noise_demo had to override it. QueerNoiseShader.gdshader's three matching constants (value x 0.770, simplex x 38.0, cellular x 0.827, perlin raw) are the family's own answer to that problem, measured by its author over 30,000 samples to a common mean |value| of 0.137, and they are taken with the functions. THE COST, said plainly: this bench's picture of `perlin` is not byte-identical to what perlin_noise or noise_terrain photograph. The constructions are shared and every structural claim transfers; the particular draw does not. And GLSL runs float32 while GDScript and the Python replica both run float64, so this file's field is not the shader's field either — a fract(sin(x) * 43758.5) hash is precision-sensitive by design. Anyone comparing this bench's simplex to noise_terrain's simplex is comparing two draws of one construction, which is the honest thing to compare and should be said out loud in the room.
declines: `generator` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, which is the decline that defines the artifact. The four values sit SIDE BY SIDE — see dna.axis_shape for the code — so an axis over them would have four values each of which demolishes three quarters of the exhibit, and the big number it produced would be measuring the exhibit being dismantled. The word is exhibited instead: all four stand in every tile, lettered on the apron, read out of noiseroom.gd's own const rather than retyped, and checked in both directions at _ready. The bench then measures what it would have measured anyway, on a homogeneous rank where all four benches carry one basis: 20.00% mean pairwise focus at K=1, 18.62% at K=2, 17.96% at K=3. That number is reported in dna.predicted_degeneracy as a finding rather than smuggled in as an axis.

A FOURTH OCTAVE RUNG. noise_space and noise_quarry both declare [1, 2, 3, 4] and this bench declares [1, 2, 3], for the reason those two gave about their own grids, re-derived on this one: at SPAN = 4 and GRID = 48 the fourth octave's lattice cell is 1.5 sample cells, below the 2-cell Nyquist wavelength, so the rung would add aliasing at a sixteenth of the amplitude and nothing a still frame can resolve. The arithmetic is in dna.kin. Refusing a rung from a shared list is the bouncing_ball move and is recorded rather than quietly done.

`readout` (relief | plate | column), THE OTHER OBVIOUS AXIS AND THE ONE THIS BENCH'S COMPANION EXHIBITS. Sweeping it would mean the body is not identical across the sheet, and 'identical sampling, identical body, so the generator is the only variable' is the design line — a bench that changes its body between tiles is comparing two things at once and can attribute neither. The body is held at `relief`, which is the family's own shipped default (perlin_noise, simplex_noise and random_edge_profile all default readout to relief) and the only one of the three that has a silhouette, which is where three of these bases swell and one has creases. The quarry already sweeps the field under all three bodies; running readout here too would make the pair redundant rather than transposed.

`accretion` (summed | single | ridged | pingpong), voxel_noise_demo's second axis. It is a real and well-named word for how the octaves are COMBINED, and it is declined because it is a FastNoiseLite word: single, ridged and pingpong are FRACTAL_NONE, FRACTAL_RIDGED and FRACTAL_PING_PONG, and this bench's fBm is fifteen lines of its own. Implementing three of them by hand would be inventing an answer for a word whose answers are an engine enum — the folding_past fault, with the artifact on the other side of it. `single` alone is reachable here and is exactly octaves=1, which is why the ladder starts there.

`legend` (contours | relief | mood), noise_terrain's second axis. It asks what the surface says its heights MEAN, and both of its non-default values are already spent here in fixed form: the colour ramp is on at every tile (that is `mood` in noise_terrain's sense, and it is the family's own ramp from NoiseVisualizer.gd:56) and there are no contour lines anywhere. Taking the word would mean either three values two of which are the same picture, or inventing a fourth to hold what actually ships.

A SEED EXPORT, and it is a decline about citation rather than about determinism. The brief asked for the family's own seeds where they exist; the family's seeds are FastNoiseLite seeds — voxel_noise_demo ships noise_seed 1337 and noise_terrain's fixture pins 20260803 — and the ported sine-hash bases have no seed at all, being pure functions of position. Transplanting 1337 into a hash that has no seed input would mean inventing a way for it to matter and then citing the family for the number, which is a fake citation. What IS taken rather than invented is the CUT: ORIGIN_U = 3.37 and ORIGIN_V = 7.91 are noise_quarry's, character for character, so the two artifacts sample the same corner of their respective lattices.

A FRAME-RELATIVE CEILING ANYWHERE. Three gauges and all three are fixed across the whole sheet. The colour ramp runs h = -1 .. +1 on every bench at every rung. The relief gauge is 2 x AMP = 0.48 m for the full range on every bench at every rung, and it is built so that h = -1 lands exactly on the apron top and h = +1 exactly on the board's lower edge. The census ceiling is 1050 counts on every bench at every rung — the largest bin anywhere in the sheet is 1006 (cellular at K=3), so nothing is clipped and nothing is rescaled to its own busiest bar. The consequences are visible and are left alone: the realised field spans 1.905 of the available 2.0 at K=1 and 1.399 at K=3, so the high rungs genuinely use less of the gauge; and cellular's census is visibly shifted up while value's is shifted down, which is the finding rather than an error to normalise away. sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

A PER-BASIS NORMALISATION ON TOP OF THE SHADER'S. The four bases are amplitude-matched by the three constants taken with their functions, and then ONE gain of 2.20 is applied to all four identically. It would have been easy to scale each bench to fill the gauge and the pictures would have been handsomer; the four would then have had four different meanings for the same colour and the same height, and the disagreement about where the middle of a field is — the second finding, and the whole subject of the census — would have been erased by the fix. Note also that because `generator` is exhibited rather than swept, all four constants are present in every single tile, so they cannot function as a per-frame normalisation even in principle.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, DURATION OR DECAY. A noise field has obvious time-domain axes — the third coordinate as a clock, a scroll, an octave fading in — and every one of them is invisible to a still PNG. Two of this family's members had to export a freeze for exactly this reason (noise_terrain's animate, shader_noise_space's `animation` fixture, which exists because every visible parameter of that room is driven off a clock in _process). There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics body anywhere in this file, so there is nothing to freeze.

AN OCCLUSION LEDGER, designed and dropped for the same reason noise_quarry dropped one. The plan was a bar per bench counting how many of the 2304 samples that crust hides from the standpoint. It was dropped when the arithmetic came back: with the same gauge, the same grid and the same body on all four benches, a horizon walk returns counts within a few per cent of each other for the three smooth bases and only cellular's cliffs stand out — and cellular's excess is a fact about cliffs, which the silhouette already says louder. Four bars, three the same length, restating the picture.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below come from building this exact geometry in Python — the same four ported bases, the same fBm, the same layout constants, the same census — rasterising it with a z-buffer at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.57) and pushing the result through that same pipeline. Subject fraction of frame: 15.67%. Crop: 666 x 277 px.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `octaves` 2 <-> 3, AT evidence=trace: 6.73% focus, 0.54% frame. It clears the critic's TWIN_FOCUS bar of 6.00% by 0.73 of a point, so I predict NO twins — and that margin is thin enough to be the thing to check first.

WHY THAT PAIR, arithmetically. The field is fBm at persistence 0.5, so octave k carries amplitude 0.5^(k-1) against a normaliser of the sum:
    K=2  last octave = 0.500 / 1.500 = 33.33% of the sum
    K=3  last octave = 0.250 / 1.750 = 14.29%
Measured over the 2304 samples of each bench, mean |dh| and the mean vertical move it produces at AMP = 0.24:
    1 -> 2   simplex 0.1335 / perlin 0.1309 / value 0.1225 / cellular 0.1304   ~31 mm
    2 -> 3   simplex 0.0537 / perlin 0.0535 / value 0.0554 / cellular 0.0478   ~13 mm
    1 -> 3   simplex 0.1534 / perlin 0.1528 / value 0.1415 / cellular 0.1468   ~36 mm
Adjacent rungs converge geometrically, so the top of the ladder is where the axis is thinnest. This is the field_room ruling and not a fault to fix: the rung is thin because the thing it describes is thin, and padding it would mean raising persistence away from the family's 0.5 to make a louder picture of a different function. Note that noise_quarry predicted its own thinnest pair for exactly this reason at exactly this persistence; two artifacts finding `octaves` weak at the top of the ladder is a fact about the word, not about either bench.

THE WHOLE PREDICTED SHEET, frame% / focus%.
  `octaves`, at each evidence rung:
    1<->2 @ result     0.85 / 10.89      1<->3 @ result     0.94 / 12.08      2<->3 @ result     0.54 /  6.77
    1<->2 @ trace      0.84 / 10.83      1<->3 @ trace      0.93 / 12.03      2<->3 @ trace      0.54 /  6.73
    1<->2 @ longhand   1.07 / 13.56      1<->3 @ longhand   1.26 / 15.88      2<->3 @ longhand   0.65 /  8.15
  `evidence`, at each octave rung:
    result<->trace     @ K=1  0.66 / 13.20    @ K=2  0.66 / 13.10    @ K=3  0.66 / 13.17
    result<->longhand  @ K=1  1.46 / 23.73    @ K=2  1.46 / 23.61    @ K=3  1.46 / 23.69
    trace<->longhand   @ K=1  0.80 / 15.97    @ K=2  0.80 / 16.02    @ K=3  0.81 / 16.09
AXIS MEANS: `evidence` 0.97% frame / 17.62% focus -> BITES. `octaves` 0.85% frame / 10.77% focus -> WEAK, 1.23 points under the critic's 12% bar, and stated as WEAK in advance rather than discovered afterwards.

`octaves` IS PREDICTED TO BE CONDITIONAL, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF OF ITS NUMBER. Group by value pair across contexts rather than by context mean, per the crossed-axes ruling: every octave pair is roughly a quarter stronger at evidence=longhand than at result or trace (10.83 -> 13.56, 12.03 -> 15.88, 6.73 -> 8.15). That is not noise. The census is the only apparatus in the artifact that responds to the field, so at `longhand` the octaves axis is being read twice — once off the crusts and once off the counts — and at the default (longhand, 1) it is at its strongest. If the sweep comes back with octaves FLAT across the three evidence rungs, the census is not being recomputed from the rebuilt field.

AND ONE NUMBER THAT IS NOT AN AXIS AT ALL, which is the artifact's own argument and the reason the whole thing exists. `generator` is exhibited, so the critic will never measure it. Measured here instead, on a HOMOGENEOUS RANK — the same scene with all four benches carrying one basis, so geometry, perspective and lighting are identical and only the basis differs — in the same currency:
                          K=1     K=2     K=3
    simplex <-> perlin   16.92   15.29   14.54
    simplex <-> value    19.44   16.96   15.84
    simplex <-> cellular 20.34   19.53   18.95
    perlin  <-> value    20.53   18.96   17.37
    perlin  <-> cellular 21.68   20.62   20.45
    value   <-> cellular 21.06   20.35   20.60
    MEAN                 20.00   18.62   17.96
Three claims fall out of that table and all three can be wrong. (1) The four bases converge as octaves are summed — monotone at the mean, and the fall is 10% over two rungs, which is real but much gentler than the eye reports, so a viewer's impression that K=3 is "all mush" overstates what the pixels say. (2) The closest generator pair is simplex <-> perlin at EVERY rung, and it is also the fastest to converge (-14% against the mean's -10%), which is what you would expect of two gradient noises differing only in the shape of their lattice. (3) Cellular stays the furthest from everything and barely converges at all (perlin <-> cellular 21.68 -> 20.45, value <-> cellular 21.06 -> 20.60, which RISES on the last rung). That last one is the headline stated as a number: three of these are smooth fields and one is a partition, and summing scales does not make a partition smooth.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If any `evidence` pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=generator_bench first — a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
(b) If `octaves` comes back near 0% while `evidence` bites, the field is not being rebuilt: apply_grid_config only calls _build() when a value actually changed AND _built is true.
(c) If BOTH axes come back roughly 1.3-1.6x these numbers, the cause is SHADING and the difference is known rather than suspected. The replica renders untextured colour with a clamped Lambert key at the rig's own -42/-35 and a fill at -20/130, an ambient term, a filmic curve and an sRGB round trip — but no shadows, no specular and no ambient occlusion. The crusts are 48 x 48 stepped tiles with skirts on all four sides, which is exactly the geometry shadows and AO bite hardest, and it is exactly where `octaves` does its work. So the replica's `octaves` figure is the more likely of the two to be low, and the WEAK verdict is the one most likely to be overturned upward.
(d) The replica does not model the four Label3D basis tabs. They are constant across all nine tiles and add roughly 0.4% more constant subject area to every crop, which dilutes both axis means slightly — in the direction of the numbers above being a little high, not a little low.
(e) If the closest pair comes back as `evidence` result<->trace instead of `octaves` 2<->3, the prediction is not wrong, it is resolved: what it resolves is whether one 5.34 m x 0.070 m blade appearing counts for more or less than every sample on four crusts moving 13 mm. The predicted gap between those two is 6.73 against 13.20, which is wide enough that a swap would mean something is wrong with the crusts rather than something is different about the light.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL NINE FRAMES, which is also the box at every individual frame. Union 5.58 x 1.06 x 2.17 (x across the four benches, y from the apron underside to the board top, z from the board to the apron's front edge); diagonal sqrt(31.1364 + 1.1236 + 4.7089) = 6.080205, radius 3.040103. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 3.040103 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 18.8931 m and show an 11.5524 m frame around a 5.58 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.57 the camera comes to 10.7691 m and the frame to 6.5849 m, which is 115.42 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting the subject's measured bounding box is 666 x 277 px of the 760 x 760 frame with 69 px of margin on the left and 25 px on the right, and it covers 15.67% of the frame. The margins are not equal and the reason is perspective, not an error: the camera stands on the +x/+z side, so the +x end of a 5.58 m apron is nearer and projects further out. The orthographic estimate — 5.58 x |right.x| + 2.17 x |right.z| = 5.58 x 0.813879 + 2.17 x 0.581037 = 5.8023 m, i.e. 88.1% of frame width with 45 px each side — is symmetric and 20 px optimistic on the near side, which is exactly the amount by which a perspective rig is not an orthographic one. 0.55 was measured too and puts the right margin at 13 px, which is too little slack for the showcase key light's specular fringe that the replica does not model; 0.58 was measured and costs 0.8 points of subject fraction for nothing. Cropping is arithmetically impossible above framing = 1 / PAD = 0.5263 because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE, so 0.57 keeps 8% of sphere margin in hand on top of the 25 measured pixels.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: it makes no difference here and that is worth stating rather than assuming. The apron (5.58 x 2.17, y 0 to 0.10) and the board (y 0.58 to 1.06) define all six faces of the box and neither moves with either axis. The datum rule lives inside them at y 0.27-0.34, z 0.849-0.871; the census bars live inside them at y 0.58-1.06, z -1.125 to -1.105; and the crusts cannot reach a bound because the gauge is built so h = -1 lands exactly on the apron top and h = +1 exactly on the board's lower edge, with the widest realised |h| in the sheet at 0.95431. All nine tiles are framed identically.

GAUGE CHECK AT 115.42 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. Horizontals use |right.x| = 0.813879 along the frame's long axis, verticals use cos(pitch) = 0.966390:
  datum rule    5.34 m long -> 501.6 px;  0.070 m tall ->  7.8 px
  census board  5.34 m long -> 501.6 px;  0.480 m tall -> 53.5 px
  census bin                              0.060 m tall ->  6.7 px
  census bar    per 100 counts 0.1143 m -> 10.7 px of length
  crust gauge   2 x AMP = 0.48 m         -> 53.5 px
  crust lip     0.035 m                  ->  3.9 px
  sample cell   0.025 m                  ->  2.4 px along x, 1.7 px along z
  basis tab     cap height 0.077 m       ->  8.6 px
THE BINS WERE SIZED FOR THE CRITIC, NOT FOR THE EYE. The crop is 666 x 277 and the critic resizes to 160 x 160, so verticals are downsampled 1.73x and a mark must clear about 5.2 screen pixels to survive as three samples. Twelve bins — the quarry's ramp-band count, which was the first choice — give 0.040 m = 4.3 px = 2.5 samples, which is under the bar; eight bins give 0.060 m = 6.7 px = 3.9 samples. Eight is enough resolution to separate the four distributions: the census counts at K=1 run [18, 185, 378, 527, 590, 372, 206, 28] for simplex against [1, 41, 231, 472, 641, 542, 315, 61] for cellular, and the difference is legible in the silhouette.

THE SAMPLE CELL IS BELOW LEGIBILITY AND IS LEFT THERE. At 0.025 m the individual tiles are 2.4 px across and 1.7 px deep, so the crust reads as a continuous hatched surface rather than as countable cells — which is what the axis needs, since the subject is the shape of the field and not the grid it was sampled on. Coarsening the grid to make cells countable would cap the octave ladder at 2 (see dna.kin); refining it to hide the hatching entirely would quadruple the vertex count. What matters is that the crust's own step size (0.025 m) is THREE TIMES FINER than the finest thing any field says (the k=3 lattice cell at 0.075 m), so the body is not adding a blockiness that competes with value noise's real one.

THE BOARD'S STANDOFF IS NOT THE QUARRY'S PROBLEM, because the board was raised instead. At the sweep's standpoint a sight line descends 0.3269 m per metre of -Z travel, so a wall at the quarry's 0.55 m of standoff is grazed by the benches' back rows: a crust peak at 0.5690 m hides everything below 0.3892 m on that wall, which would be 65% of a ruled band starting at the apron. Rather than push the board back — which costs frame width on the dimension that is already the largest — its lower edge was put at 0.58 m, the crust's own h = +1 line, where no sample can ever reach it. The board is then 0.48 m tall, exactly 2 x AMP, so the artifact reads as one continuous 0.96 m ruler: the bottom half is where the field stands and the top half is where it is counted, and a mark on the board is exactly 0.48 m above the crust height it refers to.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED KEY IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no RandomNumberGenerator, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. The four bases are pure functions of position — fract(sin(dot)) hashes with compile-time constants — so they have no state at all and two captures of one value are two photographs of one object. This is the one place where porting the shader's bases rather than calling FastNoiseLite also simplifies the harness: a FastNoiseLite bench would have needed a seed pinned through dna.fixture, as noise_terrain and voxel_noise_demo both do.

_ready IS UNGATED: it reads config metadata, validates two family lists and builds the whole bench standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR EACH. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_evidence / config_octaves metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks the ancestor chain for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_evidence / _valid_octaves, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word or an out-of-range integer keeps the standing value.

NEITHER AXIS IS A BOOL, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. `octaves` is an int and is read through int(), which accepts the string "2" a sweep would set.

BUILD COST, since it is paid at every map load. Four benches x 2304 cells, each emitting one tile quad and up to two skirt quads, plus a four-sided lip on each of the 188 perimeter cells: about 166,000 vertices through SurfaceTool in GDScript, roughly 5.3x noise_quarry. Field evaluation is 4 x 2304 x K basis calls, and cellular is the expensive one at 18 sin() per sample, so the worst case (K=3) is about 124,000 sin() calls for that bench alone. This is a build-once artifact with no _process, so the cost is a load-time spike and not a frame cost — but it is the reason GRID is 48 and not 96.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `evidence`, by construction: the apron, the board and its two posts, the four basis tabs and all four crusts. Everything that changes between the three tiles is proof apparatus, which is the axis's whole subject.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `octaves`: the apron, the board, the posts, the tabs and the datum rule. The board's tonal step stays at the census's h = 0 and the census ceiling stays at 1050, so the gauge does not move when the field does. Everything inside the four crusts changes, and so does every census bar. `octaves` should be the smaller focus number and the smaller frame number, and it is — 0.85%/10.77% against evidence's 0.97%/17.62% — because the crusts are a wide thin subject repainted everywhere while the evidence marks are bright localised apparatus.

THE FOUR BENCHES ARE NOT MEANT TO LOOK EQUALLY DIFFERENT. simplex and perlin are the closest pair at every rung (16.92% at K=1 falling to 14.54% at K=3 on a homogeneous rank) and that is correct: they are the same gradient construction on two lattices, and what separates them is the presence or absence of a preferred direction, which is a subtle thing in a still. cellular is the furthest from everything and stays there. If a viewer reports that the leftmost two benches "look the same", that is the artifact working, and the census standing behind them is the place where it says so out loud.

THE CENSUS IS THE ARTIFACT'S OWN DARK SPOT AND IT IS DRAWN, NOT HIDDEN. It is the most rigorous apparatus in the frame — a count of the same array the crust is standing on, against a ceiling fixed across the whole sheet — and it is blind to exactly the difference the artifact is named for. simplex and perlin have near-identical distributions (their K=1 counts are [18, 185, 378, 527, 590, 372, 206, 28] and [41, 160, 396, 564, 564, 405, 139, 35]) and completely different geometries. What the census CAN see is the thing no single-basis artifact can show at all: cellular's 2304 samples have mean h +0.156 and value's -0.093 on one fixed gauge, so the four bases do not agree about where the middle of a field is.

THE CENSUS IS A CENSUS, NOT AN ESTIMATE, and the difference matters at the first rung. It counts this bench's 2304 samples and claims nothing about the basis in general. At SPAN = 4 a bench cuts 16 lattice cells at octave 1, so the shape of the K=1 census is as much about which 16 cells were cut as about the construction; by K=3 it is a mixture over 16 + 64 + 256 cells and much closer to a distribution. That settling is a true reading of the octaves axis and is why the census responds to octaves at all.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are four Label3D in the artifact and they letter the four bases — simplex, perlin, value, cellular — which are present at every value of both axes. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. Billboard is disabled on all four, which also keeps LabelFramer out: it treats billboard-enabled as the hanging signal and would otherwise bolt a panel and a bezel behind each one, four slabs this bench did not ask for. Label3D is not a MeshInstance3D and does not enter the capture AABB.

THE Z-STACK, WRITTEN OUT, because operations_gallery photographed a blank slab and every stage went green. Board slab z -1.165 to -1.135. Census bars z -1.135 to -1.115, i.e. wholly in FRONT of the board and with nothing in front of them — there is deliberately no rule drawn across them, which is why the board is two-toned instead. Crusts z -0.60 to +0.60, well clear of the board and 0.55 m in front of it, and the board's lower edge is above the highest sample any crust can produce. Datum rule z 0.849 to 0.871, in front of everything, y 0.27 to 0.34; the only thing it hides is a 0.07 m band of the crusts' FRONT ROW (one row of 48), below y = 0.265 at z = 0.60, which is h < -0.31 in that row alone. Basis tabs z 0.885, in front of the datum rule and 0.09 m below its bottom edge, so they occlude nothing and nothing occludes them.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was the sweep run --staged? A 5.58 m bench is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink.
(2) Is `octaves` flat across the three evidence rungs? It should be about a quarter stronger at longhand, because the census is recomputed from the rebuilt field. Flat means the census is not being rebuilt.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The four benches rank across the frame rather than in depth, so this artifact is less standpoint-sensitive than most — but the crusts' silhouettes, which are where three bases swell and one has creases, live entirely in an oblique view, and from directly overhead the four are four colour plates and the argument is half gone. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
